scheme.step: Cr²⁺ → Cr³⁺ gives d³, a stable half-filled t₂g level, so Cr²⁺ is reducing
Mn³⁺ → Mn²⁺ gives stable half-filled d⁵, so Mn³⁺ is oxidising
[Ni(CO)₄]: Ni is 0; strong-field CO pairs the electrons to give 3d¹⁰, sp³
So it has no unpaired electrons and is diamagnetic
[NiCl₄]²⁻: Ni²⁺ is 3d⁸ and weak-field Cl⁻ does not pair the electrons, sp³
So it has two unpaired electrons and is paramagnetic
The C=O group is strongly electron-withdrawing
The conjugate base (enolate ion) is stabilised by resonance
Onto: for any y ∈ R, x = (y − 3)/4 ∈ R and f(x) = y
Conclusion: one-one and onto, so f is bijective
